question_text: When designing an immutable domain object with 12 optional validation-dependent fields, why is the Builder pattern preferred over telescoping constructors?

options.text: Telescoping constructors violate thread safety during heap allocation
The Builder avoids constructor combinatorial explosion, enforces atomic validation upon `.build()`, and prevents parameter transposition errors
Telescoping constructors prevent inheritance in all compiled languages
The Builder eliminates object allocation overhead

answer_explanation: Builders provide explicit named parameter setting, eliminate ambiguous positional parameter swapping of identical types, and centralize consistency invariant checks in `.build()`.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Builders provide explicit named parameter setting, eliminate ambiguous positional parameter swapping of identical types, and centralize consistency invariant checks in `.build()`.
